concept: coordinator-allocated rail driver operation in an autumn low-adhesion commuter cab
negative_en: plastic-looking skin, unrealistic hands, broken window geometry, over-processed retouching, impossible perspective, warped walls, 3D render look, illustration look, low resolution
prompt_en: Use case: photorealistic-natural. One original adult fictional woman rail driver actively drives an autumn commuter train under low-adhesion leaf-fall restrictions. Her professional rail-driver uniform is visibly tied to operating the train: a dark navy duty jacket, pale collared shirt, dark tie, epaulettes, and plain staff badge. She is an adult train driver seated at the active cab controls, with her hand on the traction or brake controller as she cross-checks the cab indication with route information in a route-speed cross-check phase. Through the broad windscreen, the cab indication agrees with the visible signal and track: an amber caution aspect matches an amber route marker while wet crushed leaves coat both railheads. Image 1: Her visible facial structure and long dark softly waved hair are guided only by the supplied appearance reference. Use an eye-level 35 mm three-quarter cab view linking face, control, display, signal, and rails in one diagonal line. Natural overcast window light and restrained instrument glow share one believable direction across her face, uniform, and worn console, keeping realistic adult anatomy and the complete operator-cab relationship legible.
